The Police Inspector of Jayanagara Police Station, Bengaluru has filed Police Report against the accused persons alleging that they have committed the offences punishable under Sections 120B,
342, 363, 384, 417, 420 and 506 R/w Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. It is the case of the Prosecution that the husband of the informant Eshwar Murthy was having an ancestrail and joint family property bearing its No.190/59 situated at Jayanagara, Bengaluru.
These accused by taking advantage of the addiction of the husband of the informant got registered the Sale Deed in respect of the said property.
These accused have not paid any consideration amount either to the informant or to her husband.
The said property is the ancestrail and joint family property of the informant.
The husband of the informant was also not having any right to alienate the property.

On the message of her husband the informant had been to the Police Station and lodged the information against the accused person.
3.
Based on the First Information of CW1, the crime was registered in Crime No.254/2021 at Jayanagara Police Station.
The accused persons were produced before this Court and released on bail.

On completion of the investigation, the Police Inspector of Jayanagara Police Station,
Bengaluru City filed Police Report against the accused persons alleging that they have committed the above said offences.
After taking cognizance of the said offences, the process was issued to them.
The copies of the Police Report and other prosecution papers are furnished to the accused persons under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing, since there were grounds for presuming that the accused persons have committed the offences triable by this Court, charges for the offences has been framed and read over to them in Kannada language.
They have pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
4. To prove the charges framed against the accused, the Prosecution has produced the oral evidence of PW1 and PW2 and documentary evidences as per Ex.P1 and Ex.P2.

Since, there were no incriminating circumstances appearing in the evidences of the prosecution witnesses against the Asha R vs Suresh H S on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181377114/
2 accused persons, the examination of the accused persons under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. was dispensed with.

sentences.text: 5. Heard the arguments of learned Senior Assistant Public Prosecutor and the learned counsel for the accused persons.
Perused the materials available on record.

6. The points for determination are;
1. Whether prosecution has proved beyond all reasonable doubts that the accused persons have committed the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 342, 363, 384, 417, 420 and 506 R/w Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code?
2. What order or sentence?

7. My answers to the above points are as follows:
 Point No.1 : In the Negative,
 Point No.2 : As per final order for the following:-
 REASONS 8. POINT No.1 :- It is the case of the Prosecution that these accused by playing fraud and also by taking advantage of the addiction of the informant got registered the Sale Deed in respect of the ancestral and joint family property of the husband of the informant in Sy.No.27/2 without paying any consideration amount.
9.

To prove the guilt of the accused, the Prosecution has examined CW1/PW1 Asha R., who is the informant and wife of the victim and also CW2/PW2 by name Eshwar Murthy have deposed in their evidence that they have not lodged any information against these accused.
They have not formed an illegal group and formed a criminal conspiracy and fabricated documents with the intention of usurping the property belonging to CW2.
They have not played fraud and got registered the Sale Deed in respect of their ancestral property without paying any consideration amount.
These witnesses have totally turned hostile to the case of the Prosecution.
These witnesses were cross-examined by the learned Senior APP.

But, they sticked to their own version and have deposed that the accused persons have not formed an illegal group and formed a criminal conspiracy and fabricated documents with the intention of usurping the property belonging to CW2.
They have not played fraud and got registered the Sale Deed in respect of their ancestral property without paying any consideration amount.

When the victim and the informant themselves have turned hostile, no purpose will be served in examining the rest of the witnesses and dropped all the witnesses by rejecting the prayer of the learned Senior APP.
Absolutely, there are not evidence to prove the guilt of the accused persons beyond all reasonable doubts.
Hence, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.
10. Point No.2:

In view of the Negative findings on the above Point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:-

Under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C, accused No.1 to 6 are hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 342, 363, 384, 417, 420 and 506 R/w Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code.
Their bail bonds and surety bonds will be canceled after appeal period.
